subject: Request: credit calculation for throughput loss during cross-region failover
messages:
From: Nora Ellis <n.ellis@blueharbor.com>
To: Sofia Ivanova <sofia.ivanova@redwood.com>
Cc: 
Date: Fri, 16 Apr 2027 02:30:00 +0000
Subject: Throughput drop around 2027-04-16 02:15 UTC – request for SLA credit

Hi Sofia,

We spotted a significant throughput reduction impacting our API calls routed through Redwood between 2027-04-16 02:14:30 and 02:21:45 UTC (approx 7m 15s). Our synthetic probes and production telemetry both show a ~40% drop in successful token/s throughput and a spike in tail latency during that window. This materially affected our customers in the US region.

Attached is a small KPI snapshot (request-kpi-snapshot.csv) showing error rates, p50/p95 latencies, and request counts over the 02:00–02:30 window. We also captured a sample of failed request IDs.

We believe this followed an automatic cross-region failover and would like Redwood to evaluate this against the uptime SLA and provide any applicable credit. Please confirm what you see on your side and next steps to resolve / quantify credits.

Thanks,
Nora Ellis
Director, Platform Operations
BlueHarbor Financial

From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
To: Sofia Ivanova <sofia.ivanova@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>
Cc: Nora Ellis <n.ellis@blueharbor.com>
Date: Fri, 16 Apr 2027 04:05:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Throughput drop around 2027-04-16 02:15 UTC – initial SRE analysis

Folks — quick summary of what I pulled from the runtime for the 02:14:00–02:22:00 UTC range. Full edge logs attached (edge-logs-20270416-0215.gz).

1) At 02:14:28 UTC we observed an upstream reachability fluctuation from TrafficMesh NAP-3 (their monitored incident: https://status.trafficmesh.io/incidents/2027-04-16-edge-flap). The TrafficMesh flap caused ~10–12% of proxy handshakes to hit slower fallback paths for ~90 seconds.

2) At 02:15:55 UTC Redwood's smart-routing detected increased latencies and initiated cross-region failover for the BlueHarbor route (primary: us-east-1 -> fallback: us-west-2). The routing cutover completed at 02:16:40 UTC.

3) During the 02:16:40–02:21:45 UTC window the route remained on the fallback region while we validated KV cache warmup and prefix caches; cold cache behavior and increased token generation tail explains the reduced token/s for the first ~5 minutes after the cutover. Our telemetry shows a ~35–45% throughput drop for BlueHarbor's route in that period.

Preliminary attribution: root cause chain started with TrafficMesh edge instability; Redwood's failover mitigated larger outage but introduced temporary partial degradation because of cold cache/regeneration. Per SLA Section 6.1 (third-party exceptions + failover smoothing), third-party outages that directly cause routing changes are considered for apportionment.

Proposed initial remediation path:
- Accept that TrafficMesh contributed to the event (external).
- Apply apportionment: we recommend offering a partial credit for the 02:16:40–02:21:45 window (5m 5s) where throughput was measurably degraded due to cache cold-starts after our failover. The earlier 02:14:28–02:15:55 period is attributable to TrafficMesh.

Credit calc (draft): impacted minutes = 5.083 (5m5s). Using BlueHarbor's monthly committed tokens and the per-minute SLA formula yields an estimated credit of ~0.8% of monthly invoice for that incident. If we include the TrafficMesh window under our umbrella (for goodwill), that would expand the window to ~7.25 minutes and increase credit to ~1.1%.

Attaching edge logs. Will follow up with more precise token-level billing numbers once accounting runs the job.

Jonas Weber
SRE, Redwood Inference

---
Attachment: edge-logs-20270416-0215.gz (GZ, 2.6MB)

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>
To: Nora Ellis <n.ellis@blueharbor.com>, Sofia Ivanova <sofia.ivanova@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 16 Apr 2027 08:00:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Throughput drop around 2027-04-16 02:15 UTC – proposed credit and timeline

Hi Nora — thanks for your patience while we investigated. To summarize Jonas' findings in plain terms:

- There was an upstream TrafficMesh edge flap at ~02:14:28 UTC that caused a short window of elevated errors before our routing moved traffic.
- Our automated cross-region failover completed at ~02:16:40 UTC, and the degraded throughput you saw was primarily during the ~5 minutes after the cutover while caches warmed and KV entries rehydrated.

Per our SLA and standard apportionment rules, the initial 02:14:28–02:15:55 window is attributable to TrafficMesh, and the 02:16:40–02:21:45 window is attributable to Redwood operational behavior (failover cold-start).

Proposed resolution options (please pick one):
1) Standard apportionment: apply a credit for the 5m5s Redwood-impacted window only — estimated at ~0.8% of the monthly bill (we will provide the exact invoice line once accounting completes the calc).
2) Goodwill compromise: Redwood will absorb the third-party window as well and issue a combined credit for ~1.1% of the monthly bill; we will also prioritize a follow-up runbook change to reduce cache warmup time on cross-region failovers.

If you accept the goodwill option we'll fast-track the credit and add SUP-9876 to our internal tracker to implement the runbook improvement.

Please reply with which option you'd prefer; if neither, we can schedule a quick 20m call to walk through the numbers.

Best,
Kimberly Park
Account Lead, Redwood Inference
kimberly.park@redwood.com
